title: Drowning
hpi_narrative: {{patient_name}} is a child who was submerged in water, presenting with respiratory distress, hypoxia, altered mental status after water rescue. Drowning = respiratory impairment from submersion in liquid. Outcome: death, survival with morbidity, or survival without morbidity. NOT 'near-drowning' in current terminology. Fresh water vs salt water distinction clinically irrelevant — both cause pulmonary surfactant washout → ARDS. Key: hypoxic brain injury determines prognosis. Management: ABCs, oxygen, BVM or intubation if needed. C-spine precautions if diving mechanism. CXR (pulmonary edema vs aspiration pneumonia). Rewarming if hypothermic. All drowning victims need observation — even asymptomatic can deteriorate (secondary drowning from pulmonary edema). Admit for observation. Prevention counseling.

stacks.label: ABCs / Oxygen / Airway
stacks.finding: Intubate if hypoxic, unable to protect airway.
